newsitem.title: USA: KCBT wheat ends down, near contract lows on harvest.
newsitem.headline: KCBT wheat ends down, near contract lows on harvest.

text.p: KCBT hard red winter wheat futures ended broadly lower and near their contract lows amid record volume as harvesting progressed rapidly in the Plains and yields topped expectations, traders said.
The nearby July settled at $3.37 per bushel -- just two cents above the contract low of $3.35.
Volume in KCBT wheat futures Monday was estimated at 81.35 million bushels, eclipsing the exchange's previous single-day wheat futures record volume of 79.055 million, set April 11.
Overall, KCBT wheat settled 1/2 to 12 cents per bushel lower, with September down nine cents at $3.44-1/4.
Hot, dry weather allowed harvesting to advance rapidly over the weekend in the U.S. Plains, and reported yields were exceeding state and county averages, traders said.

"The selling was more professional-related and not as much commercial-related," a KCBT trader said. "The selling was constant all day. Even when beans rallied back and Chicago tried to rebound, we ran into real good selling."
The trader said he was hearing yield estimates for Kansas in the range of 40 to 60 bushels per acre. In 1996, Kansas wheat yields averaged 34.0 million bushels an acre.

Featured players included FIMAT Futures, which bought 2.5 million December bushels and sold one million July, traders said, and Refco sold 1.6 million September and bought one million July. General Mills bought 2.1 million July.
